items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: Joe Chambers is mentioned exclusively by the [INTERVIEWER] as an example of a musician the interviewer worked with; the [INTERVIEWEE] does not mention Joe Chambers or indicate any personal interaction.

ctx.x: Well the first band that I really worked in I played with, I did a tour with John Scofield in 1978 that was my first European tour, and that was a tour. And then I was working with Dave Liebman in ’78. And that was a very, very nurturing experience for me. I was the young blood and I was playing with Dave who’d played with all my heroes, you know, Elvin Jones, Miles Davis and that band also included a fantastic trumpet player from Japan, Terumasa Hino, John Scofield was in that band and eventually it was Ron…

Yeah, I think a work in progress. I think when I started playing with really great world class musicians who I admired and it worked out between us and I got encouragement from them. You know, which is kind of what you’re saying. Steve Grossman, an amazing tenor player, and I’m just thinking about people early on, and Joe Chambers, a very respected drummer/composer and when I was working with Jeremy Steig’s band, this was like 20 years ago, and Eddie Gomez playing bass, and these people and they would compliment…
doesn’t matter what somebody’s going to write. But at that time that was a pat on the back, it was saying oh, okay, I guess I’m okay.
